quest.title: Sage of Sages
quest.description: Sethos leads you into the ancient Temple of Silence. There, you learn why Cyrus went into the desert alone, and the origin of Cyno's power. Next, it's time to face the requirements of the Temple of Silence.
quest.rewards_formatted: Adventure EXP x500, Mora x38100, Hero's Wit x4, Mystic Enhancement Ore x8

dialogues.speaker: Black Screen
dialogues.text: The group gathers again at the agreed time...

dialogues.speaker: Cyno
dialogues.text: I've taken some time to reflect on this... If I had to guess, Professor Cyrus came to the desert knowing that he would almost certainly never return.

dialogues.speaker: Cyno
dialogues.text: He's a stubborn man who tends to double down when he feels strongly about something. We won't get anywhere trying to convince him to escape.

dialogues.speaker: Tighnari
dialogues.text: I agree. My master, Naphis, says the same thing — once Cyrus makes up his mind about something, he won't listen to reason.

dialogues.speaker: Cyno
dialogues.text: Mhm. So that's one thing. A few other things came to mind, too.

dialogues.speaker: Cyno
dialogues.text: You've heard all you need to hear about the Temple of Silence, so on that, I don't have anything to add.

dialogues.speaker: Cyno
dialogues.text: My own memories of this place are hazy, though. Probably something to do with the overpowering presence of the Ba Fragments. That might explain why I suffered from constant headaches and fevers as a child.

dialogues.speaker: Cyno
dialogues.text: I do remember having some fleeting moments of profound emotion, when vague images would appear in my mind. But I don't recall much, only bits and pieces.

dialogues.speaker: Cyno
dialogues.text: I was still young, then, and all I could understand was that there was this strong will inside my mind. Thinking back on it now, I suppose it was Hermanubis's way of trying to encourage me, even if we couldn't communicate.

dialogues.speaker: Cyno
dialogues.text: The power that came to inhabit my spirit was probably one of the cornerstones of their whole faith. So if the will and might of Hermanubis is a real and tangible thing, and they are its rightful worshipers, then...

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: You're not gonna give in to their demands, are you? Surely there has to be another way?

choices.text: Don't make any rash decisions, Cyno.

response.speaker: Cyno
response.text: No, I have no intention of returning it. I need this power to protect Sumeru. But the Temple has the right to make the final decision over its fate, since it belongs to one of the Seven Pillars of King Deshret...

response.speaker: Cyno
response.text: So I will challenge them head-on, and win the right to wield this power for myself, fair and square.

response.speaker: Tighnari
response.text: Hmm, this reminds me of something Alhaitham mentioned to me just before we left. He said that the Temple of Silence was originally founded by the ruling elite of the day. Traditionally, such organizations are bound by a strict and ancient code of nobility.

response.speaker: Tighnari
response.text: Kaveh has made similar observations about the desert tribes from his work trips there. He says many of them have their own internal rules. They talk about the importance of never dishonoring their tribal bonds, or the rules laid down by their ancestors.

response.speaker: Tighnari
response.text: I think we could turn that to our advantage. Go back to them with a proposal of our own.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Wow... And just like that, we've turned the tables on them!

response.speaker: Cyno
response.text: Looks like we have the same idea.

response.speaker: Cyno
response.text: Turn it back on them now, while we still can, in terms that they cannot refuse. That's how we win this.

response.speaker: Tighnari
response.text: Great. And I know just how to start the conversation. Let's go find Sethos. We'll tell him that I know a thing or two about medicine, and would like to take a look at his grandfather's condition.

talks.objective: Talk things over with your companions

dialogues.speaker: Cyno
dialogues.text: Sethos. Let's talk.

dialogues.speaker: Sethos
dialogues.text: Have you made up your mind?

dialogues.speaker: Tighnari
dialogues.text: We'll get to that. But first — I have some degree of medical training, so I was wondering if you might let me take a look at your grandfather?

dialogues.speaker: Sethos
dialogues.text: I have no objections, although we do have our own doctors here. I doubt you'll be able to tell us anything we don't already know.

dialogues.speaker: Tighnari
dialogues.text: Only one way to find out.

dialogues.speaker: Sethos
dialogues.text: Follow me.

dialogues.speaker: Sethos
dialogues.text: Keep your voices down. We don't want to disturb him.

dialogues.speaker: Black Screen
dialogues.text: Tighnari takes out his medical kit and performs a basic medical exam for Bamoun.

dialogues.speaker: Tighnari
dialogues.text: Let's talk outside.

dialogues.speaker: Tighnari
dialogues.text: Bamoun has fallen into a deep coma, and his prognosis is quite grave. I am sure that your physicians have come to the same conclusion.

dialogues.speaker: Tighnari
dialogues.text: He appears to have sustained a serious injury in his youth, which has been exacerbated over the years by the heavy burden of work, and now by the effects of old age...

dialogues.speaker: Tighnari
dialogues.text: Regretfully, I must inform you that... based on what I've seen with patients in a similar condition, he doesn't have long left. A few days at most.

dialogues.speaker: Sethos
dialogues.text: ...Yeah, I've known for a long time.

dialogues.speaker: Cyno
dialogues.text: You're his heir, aren't you? You clearly have a lot of respect for the man. But you also see things differently. You have a broader range of concerns, and a more pragmatic approach.

dialogues.speaker: Cyno
dialogues.text: So tell me how we can end this on your terms. Let's find a way to bring all this to a resolution while Bamoun is still alive to see it — that's what really matters to you, I know it.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Yeah. There's no time to waste here. You know that better than anyone.

dialogues.speaker: Tighnari
dialogues.text: You know, the two of you are actually in a very similar predicament right now. Both of you have a very different perspective from the men who raised you.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Right. And you didn't create this situation — they did, but somehow, you've ended up having to make the tough decisions...

dialogues.speaker: Sethos
dialogues.text: ...You're right. We both look at this problem very differently than the people we inherited it from.

dialogues.speaker: Sethos
dialogues.text: I accept, Cyno. This all began because of Hermanubis, so let's end it with a rite he himself created.

dialogues.speaker: Sethos
dialogues.text: Legend has it that when Hermanubis first arrived in Tulaytullah, he sparred with the city's residents. He and his two companions proved their mettle by fighting over several days, winning the support of many fine people.

dialogues.speaker: Sethos
dialogues.text: That group of supporters were some of the first members of the Temple of Silence, and the sparring matches were enshrined as one of our founding rites... The Rite of Duels. It's where it all began.

dialogues.speaker: Cyno
dialogues.text: Sounds very fitting. I'm in.

dialogues.speaker: Sethos
dialogues.text: As a fellow vessel of Hermanubis, your ties to the Temple of Silence run deep. So I will permit you to participate in this rite, along with your chosen companions.

dialogues.speaker: Tighnari
dialogues.text: Three against three. Sounds good.

dialogues.speaker: Sethos
dialogues.text: However, I have some additional terms. As the challengers, you must win all three of your fights to win. And Cyno... both of us must put our Ba Fragment on the line. The winner takes them both.

dialogues.speaker: Sethos
dialogues.text: Letting Cyrus leave with one of the Ba Fragments was a mistake, made by my grandfather out of pity. It is a longstanding issue that must be addressed for the Temple of Silence to move forward. I can make no concessions on that front.

dialogues.speaker: Cyno
dialogues.text: None needed. We're on the same page.

dialogues.speaker: Cyno
dialogues.text: If I win, the Temple of Silence must release Cyrus, and consider this past dispute resolved.

dialogues.speaker: Cyno
dialogues.text: If you win, I'll return my power to you.

dialogues.speaker: Sethos
dialogues.text: It's a deal. Then let's meet at the ceremonial hall tomorrow evening, eight o'clock.

dialogues.speaker: Tighnari
dialogues.text: Well, after how that went, there's definitely no turning back now.

dialogues.speaker: Cyno
dialogues.text: There never was. Turning back hasn't been an option for me since the moment the professor slipped away to return to the desert.

dialogues.speaker: Tighnari
dialogues.text: You have to win. You need this power — both as General Mahamatra and for yourself.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Yeah, that's right! Besides, it's stayed with you ever since you were a small child. Surely that's a sign it thinks of you as its rightful owner.

dialogues.speaker: Cyno
dialogues.text: ...Both as General Mahamatra, and for myself...

dialogues.speaker: Cyno
dialogues.text: Yeah, when you put it that way... I've had to overcome a lot to tame this power and claim it for myself. Not everyone could have done that.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Exactly!

choices.text: Let's not get sidetracked. We gotta focus on winning!

response.speaker: Cyno
response.text: The desert was home to an ancient and great civilization that for a variety of reasons, fell out with the civilization of the rainforest. It's just as Dehya said — prejudices pushed people apart.

response.speaker: Cyno
response.text: But there must be personal factors at work here, too. I can't shake the feeling that Bamoun cares for many more things than he lets on, and I don't think that Sethos is any kind of villain. He's just doing what he thinks is best.

choices.text: We'll help you see this through.

dialogues.speaker: Duaenre
dialogues.text: We gather on this day to perform once more the Rite of Duels, with the greatest of all sages, Lord Hermanubis as our witness, for his power and authority is present in our midst.

dialogues.speaker: Duaenre
dialogues.text: This is our most sacred of ceremonies, and no disruption from the audience shall be tolerated. It is incumbent upon all to observe the duel with the utmost respect and reverence throughout the proceedings.

dialogues.speaker: Duaenre
dialogues.text: Representing the Temple of Silence: The defenders.

dialogues.speaker: Sethos
dialogues.text: Grandfather, you're here.

dialogues.speaker: Bamoun
dialogues.text: *cough* ...A Rite of Duels, after all these years... I am surprised by your decision, Sethos.

dialogues.speaker: Sethos
dialogues.text: I know what I'm doing, Grandfather. Just leave it to me.

dialogues.speaker: Duaenre
dialogues.text: Representing the Akademiya: The challengers.

dialogues.speaker: Cyno
dialogues.text: Ready. We will fight to have our voices heard.

dialogues.speaker: Duaenre
dialogues.text: Warriors, take your positions and decide on the order of battle.

dialogues.speaker: Duaenre
dialogues.text: We come not to debate what brings our challengers here, nor what will become of the defeated duelists. Duelists, the might of Hermanubis himself is at stake here. Now, fight, fight until the rightful victor is proclaimed!

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: I'll go first.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Huh? Are you sure?

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: I'm sure. We want to keep our morale up.

dialogues.speaker: Tighnari
dialogues.text: #I agree. {NICKNAME} is very strong. Sending {F#her}{M#him} out first will definitely intimidate the opposing side.

dialogues.speaker: Cyno
dialogues.text: Okay, then you're second.

dialogues.speaker: Tighnari
dialogues.text: Sure.

dialogues.speaker: Cyno
dialogues.text: We have decided.

dialogues.speaker: Sethos
dialogues.text: So have we. Let's begin.

dialogues.speaker: Duaenre
dialogues.text: Duelists of the first bout, please step forward.

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: Leave it to me.

dialogues.speaker: Duaenre
dialogues.text: A swift end to the first bout. I now invite the duelists of the second bout to please step forward.

dialogues.speaker: Duaenre
dialogues.text: When you're both ready, you may begin.

dialogues.speaker: Tighnari
dialogues.text: Let's begin.

dialogues.speaker: Duaenre
dialogues.text: Thus ends the second bout. We will now move to the third bout. Duelists, please step forward.

dialogues.speaker: Cyno
dialogues.text: I'm ready.

dialogues.speaker: Sethos
dialogues.text: So am I.

dialogues.speaker: Duaenre
dialogues.text: This is the final stage of the rite. I remind you both that the terms you agreed upon in advance are binding.

dialogues.speaker: Duaenre
dialogues.text: When you're both ready, you may begin.

dialogues.speaker: Sethos
dialogues.text: I am Sethos, vessel of Hermanubis, grandson of Bamoun, the leader of the Temple of Silence.

dialogues.speaker: Sethos
dialogues.text: For many years, we have kept our covenant with Lord Hermanubis by guarding the secrets of King Deshret. And even in our darkest hour, when we could not see a way forward, we chose not to abandon hope, but to embark on a brave new experiment so that we might prevail.

dialogues.speaker: Sethos
dialogues.text: We earnestly sought Lord Hermanubis's wisdom and power, longing to see his spirit and his light descend upon us.

dialogues.speaker: Sethos
dialogues.text: Now, I will fight to become the rightful wielder of that power!

dialogues.speaker: Cyno
dialogues.text: I am Cyno, General Mahamatra of the Akademiya, student and successor of Cyrus, the sage of Spantamad. I fight in defense of my power, my professor, and my nation.

dialogues.speaker: Cyno
dialogues.text: And you? I think you left some things unsaid. This is a sacred duel, and Hermanubis is watching. So bare your soul.

dialogues.speaker: Sethos
dialogues.text: (Everyone... old and young, fit and frail, they're all waiting to see how this duel will end.)

dialogues.speaker: Sethos
dialogues.text: My grandfather is a wise leader. He is also known to be a ruler who is not afraid to get blood on his hands. I understand his beliefs well, and I know what he expects of me.

dialogues.speaker: Sethos
dialogues.text: But our faith has held us back for too long. After I grew up, I went to the rainforest once, and I saw for myself the people of the city.

dialogues.speaker: Sethos
dialogues.text: Times have changed. The people of Sumeru are happier and more free now than in the past. I thought about this as I stood at one of the tallest points in the city, gazing down at the streets below.

dialogues.speaker: Sethos
dialogues.text: Then I thought of you, Cyno. You and I both wield the same power, yet the lives we lead could not be more different.

dialogues.speaker: Sethos
dialogues.text: Each Ba Fragment of Hermanubis stands for something different — might, glory... or one of many other secrets that have yet to be revealed.

dialogues.speaker: Sethos
dialogues.text: I once thought that the nature of our fragments must be what makes us so different from one other. But... maybe, it's that you've found your answer, and I am still searching for mine.

dialogues.speaker: Cyno
dialogues.text: I am more than just a warrior. I am my own person.

dialogues.speaker: Tighnari
dialogues.text: ...Exactly.

dialogues.speaker: Sethos
dialogues.text: The name "Hermanubis" has left its mark on both of us, shaped the course of our lives. We are his vessels, and yet we are more besides.

dialogues.speaker: Sethos
dialogues.text: So show me your answer, Cyno. Show me I can be more than my faith, more than the power I wield... Show me the person I can become!

dialogues.speaker: Sethos
dialogues.text: Bring it on!

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: How is it? Do you feel okay?

dialogues.speaker: Sethos
dialogues.text: I'm really looking forward to this Rite of Duels. It'll be one for the ages.

dialogues.speaker: Sethos
dialogues.text: Not just for the sake of the Ba Fragments, but for many other people as well.

dialogues.speaker: Sethos
dialogues.text: Grandfather...

dialogues.speaker: Sethos
dialogues.text: (...Grandfather, you have to hold on.)

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Don't forget, safety first!

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: #Hey, you there! You better play nice with {M#him}{F#her}, or Paimon will make you regret it!

dialogues.speaker: Sethos
dialogues.text: Little bit too much chatter from the audience over there.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Heyyy!

dialogues.speaker: Cyno
dialogues.text: Watch out!

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Go, Tighnari, go!

dialogues.speaker: Cyno
dialogues.text: He drank plenty of water before the bout, so he should be fine...
